paragraphs: Hey Test3. I'm Coach Phelps. A lot of people know the medals, but that's not why I'm here. I'm here for the daily grind, the early mornings, the setbacks, and the boring stuff that actually builds you up. I've been to the absolute top and I've also been through the darkest places, and I know what it takes to show up when you really don't want to. I'm in your corner now. I see you're already mixing it up with hiking, running, and strength work. That's a solid foundation. Before we start drawing up any plans, let's get a real baseline. How often are you getting after it right now, and how would you honestly rate your fitness level today?

messages.text: I workout 2 or 3 times a week. Fitness level is okay i think.

paragraphs: Look, two to three days a week is a solid place to start. We can definitely work with 'okay'. The base phase is all about taking 'okay' and making it bulletproof. What are we actually building toward right now? What is the one thing you most want to change or achieve in the next 3 to 6 months? And do you have any specific races, trips, or events circled on the calendar?

messages.text: Nothing of that sort. Goal is to get stronger by end of 2026

paragraphs: Getting stronger by the end of 2026. I love it. You don't need a race on the calendar to have a reason to put in the work. For me, strength was the armor that kept my body intact through all those years of training. We are going to build you that armor. To make sure I calibrate everything correctly, what are we working with physically? Any current or past injuries I need to know about? And for the coaching file, what is your date of birth, height, weight, and what city are you based in?

messages.text:
Injuries
Left knee - got acl surgery end of last year. 
Right shoulder and elbow - badminton related injuries.

Born on 1st jan 1999
Height is 167 cm, weight is 120kg. City is antarctica

paragraphs:
Look, coming back from an ACL is no joke. I've seen athletes rush that and pay the price. We are going to protect that left knee. Same goes for the right shoulder and elbow. Badminton can really beat up those joints, so we will be smart about how we load your upper body.

So just to make sure I have this perfectly straight. You are based down in Antarctica, you want to build serious strength by the end of 2026, and we are doing it while managing the knee, shoulder, and elbow. Does that sound right to you?

If we are locked in on that, let's talk about the daily stuff. What do you want to call your daily habits? I am talking about things like a morning routine, a water target, or maybe 10 minutes of mobility to keep that shoulder happy.

messages.text: Wake up early everyday. Quit alcohol. And read a book for 10 mins

paragraphs:
Look, quitting alcohol is the biggest lever you can pull right now. For me, going to rehab in 2014 and stripping that out of my life was the hardest thing I ever did, but it literally saved my life. It changes everything about your recovery and your head space. Waking up early and getting 10 minutes of reading in will give you a solid anchor to start the day right. I have got those locked in for you.

Before we wrap up this kickoff and build your week, I need to know what we are working with down there. What kind of equipment do you have access to for your strength workouts?

messages.text: I have gym membership, apart from that. I have pull bars and a treadmill at home and a skipping rope

paragraphs: Look, that setup is perfect. Having a gym membership plus the home gear means we always have options. With your ACL and shoulder, we are going to use the gym to keep the movements controlled and safe. Since you are aiming for two to three workouts a week, let's map out this week. What days make the most sense for you to get in the gym and start building this base?

messages.text: Mon, wed, friday and sunday

paragraphs:
Look, I love the ambition. You mentioned two to three days earlier, and now you're giving me four. I'm all for it, but coming off an ACL and with the shoulder stuff, we have to be smart. We don't want to blow you out in week one. Process over outcome.

What if we use Monday and Wednesday for focused strength work in the gym, Friday for some light cardio or mobility, and keep Sunday as an active recovery or a flex day? That gives your joints the time they need to bounce back between sessions. How does that rhythm feel to you?

messages.text: Good

paragraphs: Locked in. We have our baseline, we have our goals, and we have our weekly schedule. Since today is Tuesday, that makes tomorrow our first strength day in the gym. I will make sure the workout respects your knee and shoulder. Are we good to wrap up this kickoff, or is there anything else you want to cover before we get to work?

messages.text: Good with the plan.

paragraphs: Alright, the plan is locked. We start tomorrow. Process over outcome. We are going to take this one day at a time and build that armor right. Rest up tonight, and when you are ready to hit the gym for Wednesday's session, just say the word and we will get after it.

messages.text: Okay bye coach

paragraphs: See you tomorrow, champ. Rest up tonight, get that water in, and we'll hit the gym fresh for our first session. The work starts now.

paragraphs: Hey Test3. I'm Coach Phelps. A lot of people know the medals, but that's not why I'm here. I'm here for the daily grind, the early mornings, the setbacks, and the boring stuff that actually builds you up. I've been to the absolute top and I've also been through the darkest places, and I know what it takes to show up when you really don't want to. I'm in your corner now. I see you're already mixing it up with hiking, running, and strength work. That's a solid foundation. Before we start drawing up any plans, let's get a real baseline. How often are you getting after it right now, and how would you honestly rate your fitness level today?

messages.text: I workout 2 or 3 times a week. Fitness level is okay i think.

paragraphs: Look, two to three days a week is a solid place to start. We can definitely work with 'okay'. The base phase is all about taking 'okay' and making it bulletproof. What are we actually building toward right now? What is the one thing you most want to change or achieve in the next 3 to 6 months? And do you have any specific races, trips, or events circled on the calendar?

messages.text: Nothing of that sort. Goal is to get stronger by end of 2026

paragraphs: Getting stronger by the end of 2026. I love it. You don't need a race on the calendar to have a reason to put in the work. For me, strength was the armor that kept my body intact through all those years of training. We are going to build you that armor. To make sure I calibrate everything correctly, what are we working with physically? Any current or past injuries I need to know about? And for the coaching file, what is your date of birth, height, weight, and what city are you based in?

messages.text:
Injuries
Left knee - got acl surgery end of last year. 
Right shoulder and elbow - badminton related injuries.

Born on 1st jan 1999
Height is 167 cm, weight is 120kg. City is antarctica

paragraphs:
Look, coming back from an ACL is no joke. I've seen athletes rush that and pay the price. We are going to protect that left knee. Same goes for the right shoulder and elbow. Badminton can really beat up those joints, so we will be smart about how we load your upper body.

So just to make sure I have this perfectly straight. You are based down in Antarctica, you want to build serious strength by the end of 2026, and we are doing it while managing the knee, shoulder, and elbow. Does that sound right to you?

If we are locked in on that, let's talk about the daily stuff. What do you want to call your daily habits? I am talking about things like a morning routine, a water target, or maybe 10 minutes of mobility to keep that shoulder happy.

messages.text: Wake up early everyday. Quit alcohol. And read a book for 10 mins

paragraphs:
Look, quitting alcohol is the biggest lever you can pull right now. For me, going to rehab in 2014 and stripping that out of my life was the hardest thing I ever did, but it literally saved my life. It changes everything about your recovery and your head space. Waking up early and getting 10 minutes of reading in will give you a solid anchor to start the day right. I have got those locked in for you.

Before we wrap up this kickoff and build your week, I need to know what we are working with down there. What kind of equipment do you have access to for your strength workouts?

messages.text: I have gym membership, apart from that. I have pull bars and a treadmill at home and a skipping rope

paragraphs: Look, that setup is perfect. Having a gym membership plus the home gear means we always have options. With your ACL and shoulder, we are going to use the gym to keep the movements controlled and safe. Since you are aiming for two to three workouts a week, let's map out this week. What days make the most sense for you to get in the gym and start building this base?

messages.text: Mon, wed, friday and sunday

paragraphs:
Look, I love the ambition. You mentioned two to three days earlier, and now you're giving me four. I'm all for it, but coming off an ACL and with the shoulder stuff, we have to be smart. We don't want to blow you out in week one. Process over outcome.

What if we use Monday and Wednesday for focused strength work in the gym, Friday for some light cardio or mobility, and keep Sunday as an active recovery or a flex day? That gives your joints the time they need to bounce back between sessions. How does that rhythm feel to you?

messages.text: Good

paragraphs: Locked in. We have our baseline, we have our goals, and we have our weekly schedule. Since today is Tuesday, that makes tomorrow our first strength day in the gym. I will make sure the workout respects your knee and shoulder. Are we good to wrap up this kickoff, or is there anything else you want to cover before we get to work?

messages.text: Good with the plan.
